items.title: The operational cost of secrets sprawl: Forrester Total Economic Impact™ study
items.summary: Investment is all about measuring risk vs reward. When it comes to investing in cybersecurity solutions, the principle of “high risk, high reward” is more true than ever; the greatest rewards come from governing the highest and most pressing risks facing your company. Unfortunately, even though developer secrets pose extreme and severe risks when compromised, managing them has long been difficult. The sprawl of unmanaged or hardcoded credentials like API keys and access tokens has grown drastically over the years, and the growing use of AI tools and agents is only accelerating the issue. To quantify the potential business impact of addressing this problem, 1Password commissioned Forrester Consulting to study 1Password Enterprise Password Manager. The study examined the benefits, costs, and risks of centralizing and governing credentials across a composite global organization. Key findings from The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager: Improved developer productivity : saved an average of 165 minutes per developer per month on credential-related activities, a benefit worth approximately $864,000 over three years. Reduced risk : see a 20% reduction in addressable credential-related breach exposure, a benefit worth approximately $158,000 in over three years. Overall financial impact : 155% ROI, $1.2 million in NPV, and approximately $2.0 million in risk-adjusted value over three years. Forrester interviewed four decision-makers with experience using Enterprise Password Manager and aggregated their experiences into a composite global organization with 3,000 employees, including approximately 300 developers. Results were risk-adjusted and may vary by organization. Read the full study to learn more. Read on to learn more of what the study reveals about the benefits of governing developer secrets access across an organization. What does secrets management provide an organization? 1Password believes the greatest insight of Forrester’s study to be that 1Password EPM’s secrets management capabilities enable and empower developer and IT teams to work more efficiently. Reduced risk Prior to using 1Password EPM, Forrester’s interviewees said that they relied on fragmented systems, including legacy or browser-based password managers, spreadsheets, and shared documents. 1Password’s own research finds that 71% of organizations’ technical employees use unsecure methods of handling secrets and non-human identities (NHIs). Those methods include storing them in env. files, sharing them over Slack or other messaging tools, and even hardcoding them directly into code repositories. When a single stolen API or master key can be used by attackers to run up $600,000 in AI credits or worse, compromise your software supply chain , it’s imperative that businesses centralize their credential governance to ensure that developer secrets stay governed from a single source of truth. 1Password EPM includes developer tools to manage SSH and Git workflows without slowing down development. Developers can automatically fetch secrets into their CI/CD pipeline, CLI tools, and applications. Use the 1Password CLI, service accounts, or SDKs to inject secrets directly where you need them—no manual copy/paste or risky .env files. As Forrester found in The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager, organizations realized a 20% overall reduction in addressable credential-related breach exposure. They calculate this benefit as being worth approximately $158,000 over three years . “The composite organization improves credential governance by centralizing password storage, increasing visibility into credential risks, and strengthening access controls.” – Forrester Consulting, The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager More time for IT The number of exposed secrets is growing exponentially, and the distributed legacy systems used by many companies have left IT and Security teams unable to find or remediate those ungoverned secrets exposures. Forrester’s study found that 1Password EPM saved vital time for IT teams by driving a 70% reduction in credential-related tickets, and a 35% reduction in the effort required to handle credential-related tickets. As they put it, this allows “...IT personnel to redirect time from routine credential support to higher-value priorities.” Forrester estimates the value of this time as being worth approximately $190,000 over three years. “At 100% implementation, password-manager-related tickets became effectively negligible. Before the move, they were consistently one of the top ticket drivers for IT.” –CISO, e-commerce Increased developer efficiency Unmanaged developer credentials have been a consistent and ever-growing risk for years now. The core of the issue lies in the fact that developers face incredibly high pressure to push code quickly, but haven’t traditionally been provided with the tools needed to make their workflows both fast and secure. Forrester interviewees who had adopted 1Password EPM found that EPM’s accessibility is key to security, helping developers stay more secure while also staying more productive. In short, a given developer will save an average of 165 minutes per month on credential-related activities. Depending on the number of developers at an organization, this time saved will provide a benefit worth approximately $864,000 in over three years. “Interviewees… described improved developer satisfaction because secure credential and secrets management could be integrated into existing tools and processes rather than creating additional work. Several interviewees noted that the solution helped developer teams adopt secure practices without feeling constrained by security controls.” -The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager Legacy credential management introduces both risk and friction into developer workflows through manual requests, locally stored secrets, and other issues. The Forrester study states that, “These practices increased manual effort and created security concerns as interviewees’ organizations expanded their use of application programming interfaces, automated pipelines, and lightweight development workflows.” 1Password’s developer tools enable developers to make sure that secrets stay both governed and accessible. For instance, “ secret references ” enable developers to store and encrypt secrets within 1Password, but still load them into environment variables, configuration files, and scripts, without exposing plaintext secrets in code. They can also access secrets through the 1Password CLI and SDKs, and even use local desktop authentication such as biometrics. “Developers can retrieve credentials dynamically at runtime without storing them locally, sending them through email, or embedding them into scripts. That improves both productivity and security.” –AI and security leader, financial services How can businesses start seeing value from 1Password EPM? The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager found that 1Password EPM has a total ROI of 155%, with a net present value (NPV) of $1.2 million. The key to those figures lies in the fact that 1Password reduces risk while enabling and streamlining access workflows for developers, AI agents, and other users. For developers, 1Password provides secure workflows that don’t slow down development , letting developers save valuable time that they can better spend on building and deploying software. Unfortunately, even though developer secrets pose extreme and severe risks when compromised, managing them has long been difficult. The sprawl of unmanaged or hardcoded credentials like API keys and access tokens has grown drastically over the years, and the growing use of AI tools and agents is only accelerating the issue.

To quantify the potential business impact of addressing this problem, 1Password commissioned Forrester Consulting to study 1Password Enterprise Password Manager. The study examined the benefits, costs, and risks of centralizing and governing credentials across a composite global organization.

Key findings from The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager:

  • Improved developer productivity: saved an average of 165 minutes per developer per month on credential-related activities, a benefit worth approximately $864,000 over three years.

  • Reduced risk: see a 20% reduction in addressable credential-related breach exposure, a benefit worth approximately $158,000 in over three years.

  • Overall financial impact: 155% ROI, $1.2 million in NPV, and approximately $2.0 million in risk-adjusted value over three years.

Forrester interviewed four decision-makers with experience using Enterprise Password Manager and aggregated their experiences into a composite global organization with 3,000 employees, including approximately 300 developers. Results were risk-adjusted and may vary by organization.

Read the full study to learn more.

Read on to learn more of what the study reveals about the benefits of governing developer secrets access across an organization.

What does secrets management provide an organization?

1Password believes the greatest insight of Forrester’s study to be that 1Password EPM’s secrets management capabilities enable and empower developer and IT teams to work more efficiently.

Reduced risk

Prior to using 1Password EPM, Forrester’s interviewees said that they relied on fragmented systems, including legacy or browser-based password managers, spreadsheets, and shared documents. 1Password’s own research finds that 71% of organizations’ technical employees use unsecure methods of handling secrets and non-human identities (NHIs). Those methods include storing them in env. files, sharing them over Slack or other messaging tools, and even hardcoding them directly into code repositories.

When a single stolen API or master key can be used by attackers to run up $600,000 in AI credits or worse, compromise your software supply chain, it’s imperative that businesses centralize their credential governance to ensure that developer secrets stay governed from a single source of truth.

1Password EPM includes developer tools to manage SSH and Git workflows without slowing down development. Developers can automatically fetch secrets into their CI/CD pipeline, CLI tools, and applications. Use the 1Password CLI, service accounts, or SDKs to inject secrets directly where you need them—no manual copy/paste or risky .env files.

As Forrester found in The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager, organizations realized a 20% overall reduction in addressable credential-related breach exposure. They calculate this benefit as being worth approximately $158,000 over three years.

“The composite organization improves credential governance by centralizing password storage, increasing visibility into credential risks, and strengthening access controls.”

– Forrester Consulting, The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager

More time for IT

The number of exposed secrets is growing exponentially, and the distributed legacy systems used by many companies have left IT and Security teams unable to find or remediate those ungoverned secrets exposures.

Forrester’s study found that 1Password EPM saved vital time for IT teams by driving a 70%

reduction in credential-related tickets, and a 35% reduction in the effort required to handle credential-related tickets. As they put it, this allows “...IT personnel to redirect time from routine credential support to higher-value priorities.”

Forrester estimates the value of this time as being worth approximately $190,000 over three years.

“At 100% implementation, password-manager-related tickets became effectively negligible. Before the move, they were consistently one of the top ticket drivers for IT.”

–CISO, e-commerce

Increased developer efficiency

Unmanaged developer credentials have been a consistent and ever-growing risk for years now. The core of the issue lies in the fact that developers face incredibly high pressure to push code quickly, but haven’t traditionally been provided with the tools needed to make their workflows both fast and secure.

Forrester interviewees who had adopted 1Password EPM found that EPM’s accessibility is key to security, helping developers stay more secure while also staying more productive.

In short, a given developer will save an average of 165 minutes per month on credential-related activities. Depending on the number of developers at an organization, this time saved will provide a benefit worth approximately $864,000 in over three years.

“Interviewees… described improved developer satisfaction because secure credential and secrets management could be integrated into existing tools and processes rather than creating additional work. -The Total Economic Impact™ Of 1Password Enterprise Password Manager

Legacy credential management introduces both risk and friction into developer workflows through manual requests, locally stored secrets, and other issues. For developers, 1Password provides secure workflows that don’t slow down development, letting developers save valuable time that they can better spend on building and deploying software.
